title: Original application state owner construction and transition

0x4f63ec.name: operator new
0x4f63ec.reason: the C runtime heap ends in operating-system calls

0x546d5c.name: SetRect
0x546d5c.reason: Win32 rectangle service: write left, top, right, bottom in argument order and return nonzero.

0x546df0.name: timeGetTime
0x546df0.reason: WinMM clock service: return the case-controlled unsigned millisecond tick without changing game objects.

0x5469e4.name: lstrlenA
0x5469e4.reason: Win32 string service: return the byte count before NUL (zero for a null pointer), without modifying the string.

0x5469e8.name: InterlockedDecrement
0x5469e8.reason: Win32 atomic service: subtract one modulo 2^32 from the pointed word, store it, and return the new word.

0x5469ec.name: InterlockedIncrement
0x5469ec.reason: Win32 atomic service: add one modulo 2^32 to the pointed word, store it, and return the new word.

0x546d54.name: ShowCursor
0x546d54.reason: Win32 cursor service: increment or decrement a case-controlled display counter according to the Boolean argument and return its signed new value; hide loops must eventually receive a negative count.

0x546cd8.name: SetCursor
0x546cd8.reason: Win32 cursor service: set the case-controlled cursor handle and return the previous handle.

0x546ce4.name: GetAsyncKeyState
0x546ce4.reason: Win32 keyboard service: return the case-controlled key-state SHORT in EAX, preserving down and pressed-since-last-query bits.

0x546c44.name: GetSystemMetrics
0x546c44.reason: Win32 display service: return the case-controlled signed metric for the requested index; reset paths query screen width and height.

0x546d9c.name: SetCursorPos
0x546d9c.reason: Win32 cursor service: record the signed screen coordinates in service state and return the case-controlled success Boolean.

limits: operator new and operator delete use synthetic allocation and release; allocation success and failure are controlled by cases.
SetRect is an exact memory-writing service stand-in; no host rectangle API is invoked.
lstrlenA and InterlockedIncrement/InterlockedDecrement use their string-length and pointed-word semantics; CString and other game/CRT callees continue to execute original instructions.
timeGetTime uses a controlled millisecond clock; timing prefixes stopped at this service establish construction coverage only.
ShowCursor and SetCursor use controlled cursor state, and input reset uses controlled GetAsyncKeyState, GetSystemMetrics and SetCursorPos services.

Cases must supply valid retained-state, resource-directory and owner-service records; construction-prefix coverage and missing-resource failures do not establish playable startup, menu, level loading or results.
notes: Full application-state transition boundary, including all concrete switch types, retention and cleanup, allocation failures, initialization outcome, activation and input reset. The return is a Boolean consumed by original callers. No game callee is replaced and no switch arm is excluded.
